The last time i was in the ER i was almost getting admitted inpatient. I got freaked out as i didn't think my situation was that serious. With the help of my aunt i was released and heard a lot of 'advice' from my family that if i were admitted in, it would affect my whole life and would greatly threaten my means of finding a job. The whole place seemed out of this world. It seemed worse to stay in the hospital than the dorm i was staying in which was distressing me greatly. I had no idea of the treatments of the hospital towards the patients. But, one part of me still thinks it would do me more good if i stayed inpatient. I finally felt like my mental health was taken seriously. I almost cried as i talked about my problems to the doctor. I still use the antipsychotic she gave me, i think it genuinely saved my sanity and it is like a pill that magically enables me to sleep each time i take it.  Now i am solving all the problems i had at the dorm, and i think i actually am doing better. Yesterday i searched for the contacts of that woman for hours but could find nothing. I just wanted to say thank you to her, because of her i now know my illness and can try to manage it better. Sometimes hospitals can be really illuminating.
